title: How fast are LLM inference engines anyway? — Charles Frye, Modal
talk_summary: Charles Frye presents Modal's LLM Almanac, a benchmark of open-weight models (Qwen3, Gemma3, Llama) across vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM at varying context lengths, showing throughput/latency tradeoffs. The core empirical finding is that prefill-heavy workloads (long input, short output) are ~4x faster than decode-heavy ones, and that context is a cheaper quality lever than reasoning.

takeaways.technique: Prefer context over reasoning for quality gains
takeaways.what_they_do: When a product wants higher quality, they add more input context rather than switching to reasoning/thinking models, because prefill is parallel and cheap while decode is serial and expensive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't immediately reach for reasoning. Reach for context instead because it's going to be cheaper
takeaways.numbers: ~4x higher requests/sec for 1024-in/128-out vs 128-in/1024-out; time-to-first-token nearly identical (~400ms) despite 10x more input tokens

takeaways.technique: Precompute a benchmark matrix instead of ad-hoc queries
takeaways.what_they_do: They answered repeated 'how fast is X model on Y engine' questions by running a giant benchmark over ~10 models x ~10 context lengths x 3 engines and publishing a queryable page with raw data and open-source harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: compute the thing ahead of time and store it
takeaways.numbers: Ad-hoc answer time went from days to 1-2 hours to 15-20 minutes, then to zero via precomputed results

takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish arithmetic-heavy parallel work (prefill, big matmuls) from memory/communication-bound serial work (decode) and steer workloads toward the former.
takeaways.numbers: 4x throughput difference between prefill-dominated and decode-dominated workloads

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure throughput per single GPU replica and note total throughput comes from scaling replicas horizontally, with queuing theory predicting latency blowup past max RPS.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the way you solve your like total throughput is by scaling out rather than scaling up
takeaways.numbers: ~1 request/sec per H100 replica on Qwen3 MoE at 128-in/1024-out
